## User-AI Interaction requirements:
- Always ask me before installing any dependencies or packages.  
- If you comment, please comment in the structure # NOTE(copilot): <your comment here> to make it clear that the comment is generated by copilot. In contrast, I will use the structure # NOTE(m): <my comment here> for my comments.
- I will do the git commits, so please do not commit any code. However, you can ask me to commit code after you have generated it and think this is a good moment.
- Use models from the Antropic Claude family for all AI tasks. 

## Context of the code in this repository:
- This repository is a supporting document for a dataset publication. The preprint of the publication is accessible under arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03521. The dataset is published on Zenodo under: https://zenodo.org/records/17831177. 
- The goal of this respository is to facilitate other researchers to explore the dataset. It should comprise: 
    - code to automatically download the data from Zenodo (all at once or parts of them) 
    - code to load the data into memory based on different parameters including the joining functionality based on the columns feeder and timestamp_UTC / date
    - code to train a simple model on the data to do forecasts or to generate pseudo-measurements. The focus is on a simple baseline with a simple model. 
- Entry points for users: there should be a main.py file with a basic example which downloads the data, loads it into memory and makes a small forecast. Furthermore there should be a notebook in a tutorial style which explains how to use the code and explore the data.

## Coding requirements
- Use python 3.12 for the application.
- Preferebly, use polars for data processing and only convert to pandas/numpy if the library, e.g. for a model training, does not support polars. Use polars dataframes and not polars lazyframes.
- Use only UV for dependency management and packaging.
- Use git version control. 
- Do not make excessive comments. 
- The code should be clean, well-structured and good to understand. The code should be structured in meaningful functions which encapsulate a specific funtionality each. The focus is on easy usability for researchers who want to explore the dataset which will be loaded from Zenodo. 
- Evolution scenario: the repository should be extensible for researchers to explore the data. However, the core should be minimal and only include the necessary code for loading the data, doing basic data processing and training a simple model. The repository should be structured in a way that it is easy to add new features and functionalities in the future, e.g. by adding new folders for new models or new data processing steps.
- Follow the following structure for the files: add all code in a src/ folder.
- There is one src/tests folder for unit tests. You can use pytest for testing.
